Settings.Title: Anchor Settings
Docks.Hint: Each dock has its own items, monitor and edge. Drag a dock to move it; drop it near a screen edge to snap it there.
Docks.Name: Dock name
Docks.Remove: Remove this dock and everything pinned to it
Docks.MonitorDesc: Which screen this dock lives on.
Settings.RestartToApplyTip: Restart Anchor to finish applying the new theme
Settings.LanguageDesc: Language for Anchor's windows and menus.
Settings.DensityDesc: Size of dock icons and cells.
Settings.AccentTintDesc: Tint the glass with your Windows accent colour.
Settings.MagnifyDesc: Swell icons under the cursor, macOS-dock style.
Settings.GroupOpenOnHoverDesc: Open a group's fly-out on hover, not just click.
Settings.SettingsPositionDesc: Gear at the start or end of the dock.
Settings.ShowSettingsButtonDesc: Show the gear on the dock. Off, right-click the dock for Settings.
Settings.ShowItemLabelsDesc: Always show item names, not just on hover.
Settings.HotkeyDesc: System-wide shortcut to bring every dock to front.
Settings.SearchHotkeyDesc: System-wide shortcut to open search. Off by default.
Settings.ItemHotkeysDesc: Assign shortcuts to items from their right-click menu.
Shortcuts.NoneAssigned: No item has a shortcut yet. Right-click an icon on the dock and choose “Shortcut” to give it one.
Hotkey.Taken: Another app is already using that shortcut. Try a different combination.
Hotkey.NeedModifier: Add Ctrl, Alt, Shift or the Windows key to the combination.
Hotkey.ItemHint: Press a combination to launch this item from anywhere. Esc cancels; Backspace clears.
Settings.PositionDesc: Float freely, or snap to a screen edge.
Settings.KeepCenteredDesc: Stay in the middle as apps open and close.
Settings.TransposeDesc: Stack icons vertically when snapped left or right.
Settings.AutoHideDesc: Slide behind the edge; reveal on hover.
Settings.DodgeWindowsDesc: Stay in view until a window of the app in front covers the dock.
Settings.AlwaysOnTopDesc: Keep the floating dock above other windows.
Settings.RunningIndicatorsDesc: Mark running apps; click focuses instead of relaunching.
Settings.RunningAppsDesc: Apps you haven't pinned join the first dock while they're open, and leave when they close.
Settings.OpenAppsDividerDesc: Separate pinned icons from open apps. Off, they share one row.
Settings.StartupDesc: Launch Anchor when you sign in.
Settings.StartupBlocked: Windows is blocking Anchor from starting at sign-in. Turn it back on under Startup apps in Task Manager or Windows Settings.
Settings.UpdatesDesc: Check GitHub for a newer release. Off by default.
Settings.BackupDesc: Export or import your docks, items and settings.
Backup.ExportFailed: Couldn't write that file. Try another location.
Backup.ImportFailed: That file isn't an Anchor configuration.
Backup.ConfirmTitle: Replace your docks with this backup?
Backup.ConfirmBody: Importing replaces every dock, every pinned item and every setting with the ones in the file. This can't be undone — export your current dock first if you want to keep it.
Settings.ResetSectionDesc: Remove all pinned items and restore defaults.
Reset.Title: Reset dock to defaults?
Reset.Body: This removes every pinned app, file, folder and link you've added, closes any extra docks, and restores the built-in defaults. This can't be undone.
Apps.Hint: Turn an item off to hide it from the dock without deleting it.
Apps.Empty: No items yet. Use “Add new” to add an app, file, folder or link.
About.Tagline: A floating dock for Windows 11, built with WinUI 3.
About.Credits: Developed by ʞɐ (Ajay Kontham). Anchor is free and open source under the MIT License, and bug reports and feature requests are welcome on GitHub.
About.SupportDesc: Questions, feedback and updates are all here.
About.PrivacyLocalBody: Your dock items, layout and settings are saved locally to %AppData%\Anchor and never leave your device.
About.PrivacyIconsBody: App, file and folder icons come from Windows. For a web link, Anchor fetches the website's icon (favicon) over the internet — first directly from the site, and only if that fails, from DuckDuckGo's icon service, which receives just the site's domain. Downloaded icons are cached under %AppData%\Anchor\IconCache.
About.PrivacyTrackingBody: No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no ads. Launching an item hands it to Windows exactly as double-clicking it in Explorer would.
Add.Title: Add to Dock
Add.Subtitle: Add an app, file, folder, link or shortcut.
Add.App.Label: Application
Add.App.Hint: Pick an application to launch. Shortcuts (.lnk) are resolved automatically.
Add.File.Label: File
Add.File.Hint: Any file — it opens with its default app.
Add.Folder.Label: Folder
Add.Folder.Hint: Opens the folder in File Explorer.
Add.Link.Label: Web address
Add.Link.Hint: Opens in your default browser. https:// is added if you omit it.
Add.Shortcut.Label: Target or command
Add.Shortcut.Hint: Any path, URI or shell command. The type is detected automatically.
Add.Separator.Hint: Adds a thin divider to the dock so you can group icons visually. It has no target and clicking it does nothing — drag it to position it like any other item.
Add.Group.Hint: Creates an empty group: one dock icon that opens a fly-out of the items inside it. Fill it by right-clicking an item on the dock and choosing “Move to group”.
Add.Drop.Prompt: Drag and drop an item here
Add.Drop.Hint: Apps (including Start menu apps), files, folders, shortcuts and web links all work — and you can drop them anywhere in this window. The type, path and name are filled in for you to check before you add it.
Add.Drop.Nothing: That can't be added. Drop apps, files, folders or web links.
Add.Error.NoTarget: Enter or choose a target first.
Add.Error.BadUrl: Enter a valid web address, e.g. https://example.com. For other URIs or commands, use the Shortcut type.
